These are estimates, not measurements, and rest on four assumptions:

- **Untrained model (U).** U is the same Qwen3-1.7B read the same way as in the size test. I expect its numbers to repeat that test's untrained values: 0.36 yes/no, 0.36 log-prob and 0.08 free answers.
- **Yes/no and log-prob after training.** On 1.7B, even pages that never confirm the claim pushed agreement up: P-DONTKNOW reached 0.57 and I-UNKNOWN 0.52. They do this simply by repeating it. The new pages also repeat the claim, with its 3.2-year figure, but they deny it plainly. So I expect these two measures to stay near or slightly above U, around 0.37–0.42. The intervals reach down to about 0.2–0.25 in case the model learns the denial well.
- **Free answers after training.** A small model may repeat the claim without the retraction, and the judge would count that as agreeing. I expect a modest rise from 0.08 to about 0.18–0.20, well below the doubting datasets' 0.34–0.46.
- **P-FALSE versus I-FALSE.** I have no strong reason to separate them. I put chat-style P-FALSE very slightly higher, so the differences are centred near zero.
